<a id="ia.server-rendered-content"></a>

### 3.1 Server-side rendered content

- Stable ID: `ia.server-rendered-content`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: MUST
- AR practices: AR-READ-01, AR-READ-03 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `measured_study`
- Fix: Render the main content in the HTML response, without JavaScript.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.server-rendered-content)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-01](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Pass condition: Meaningful text content in the initial HTML response
- Expected result: The HTML response contains the main headings and body text
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.server-rendered-content`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.server-rendered-content

Why: Fetch-only crawlers and non-rendered retrieval cannot depend on client-side JavaScript. Browser agents may combine the rendered DOM, accessibility tree, and screenshots. Meaningful server-rendered HTML keeps core content available across both access modes.

References:

- [Build agent-friendly websites](https://web.dev/articles/ai-agent-site-ux) (guide)
- [Google JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) (guide)

Steps:

1. Fetch the page without JavaScript and compare the text with the rendered page.
2. Enable server-side rendering or static generation for the main content.
3. Keep headings, body text and links in the initial HTML.

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/
```

<a id="ia.heading-hierarchy"></a>

### 3.2 Heading hierarchy

- Stable ID: `ia.heading-hierarchy`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: MUST
- AR practices: AR-READ-03 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Use one h1 and do not skip heading levels.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.heading-hierarchy)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-03](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.heading-hierarchy`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.heading-hierarchy

Why: AI agents use headings to build a content outline and determine topic hierarchy. A clear h1→h2→h3 structure helps AI systems extract and summarize your content accurately.

References:

- [MDN Heading Elements](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/Heading_Elements) (guide)
- [W3C Using h1-h6 to identify headings](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H42) (spec)

Steps:

1. Give each page one h1 that names the main topic.
2. Use h2 for sections and h3 for subsections, without skipped levels.

   ```html
   <h1>Pricing</h1>
   <h2>Plans</h2>
   <h3>Team plan</h3>
   ```

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

### 3.3 Semantic HTML elements

- Stable ID: `ia.semantic-html`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: MUST
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Use main, nav, header, footer and article for the page structure.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.semantic-html)
- Evidence source: [MDN Semantics in HTML](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Semantics#semantics_in_html)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.semantic-html`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.semantic-html

Why: Browser agents may combine the DOM, accessibility tree, and screenshots. Semantic elements like <main>, <nav>, and <article> provide durable structural meaning across those representations.

References:

- [MDN Semantics in HTML](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Semantics#semantics_in_html) (guide)
- [W3C HTML5 Document Sections](https://www.w3.org/TR/html52/sections.html) (spec)

Steps:

1. Replace layout div elements with semantic elements.

   ```html
   <header>...</header>
   <nav>...</nav>
   <main>
     <article>...</article>
   </main>
   <footer>...</footer>
   ```
2. Use one main element per page.

### 3.4 Landmarks and ARIA

- Stable ID: `ia.landmarks-aria`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Give each page region a landmark and label repeated landmarks.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.landmarks-aria)
- Evidence source: [W3C Landmarks Pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/landmarks/)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.landmarks-aria`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.landmarks-aria

Why: ARIA landmarks help AI agents identify page regions (navigation, main content, footer). This is the same API used by screen readers and is increasingly used by AI browsing agents.

References:

- [W3C Landmarks Pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/landmarks/) (guide)
- [MDN ARIA Roles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles) (guide)

Steps:

1. Make sure that each page has a main, a navigation and a contentinfo landmark.
2. Add aria-label when a landmark type occurs more than once.

   ```html
   <nav aria-label="Main">...</nav>
   <nav aria-label="Footer">...</nav>
   ```

- Strength: MUST
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)

<a id="ia.form-labels"></a>

### 3.9 Form label coverage

- Stable ID: `ia.form-labels`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Give each form field a visible label that is linked with for and id.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.form-labels)
- Evidence source: [WCAG Labels or Instructions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.form-labels`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.form-labels

Why: AI agents interact with forms via the accessibility tree, which maps labels to inputs. Without proper label associations, AI agents cannot determine what data a form field expects, making form interaction unreliable or impossible.

References:

- [WCAG Labels or Instructions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html) (spec)
- [MDN label element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/label) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add a label element for each input, select and textarea.

   ```html
   <label for="email">Email</label>
   <input id="email" name="email" type="email">
   ```
2. Use aria-label only when a visible label is not possible.

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

### 3.10 Form field autocomplete

- Stable ID: `ia.form-autocomplete`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Add autocomplete tokens to personal data fields.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.form-autocomplete)
- Evidence source: [WHATWG Autofill](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#autofill)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.form-autocomplete`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.form-autocomplete

Why: The autocomplete attribute tells AI agents and browsers what type of data a field expects (email, name, address). This semantic hint helps AI agents fill forms accurately without guessing field purposes from visual context.

References:

- [WHATWG Autofill](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#autofill) (spec)
- [WCAG Identify Input Purpose](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/identify-input-purpose.html) (spec)

Steps:

1. Add the matching WHATWG autocomplete token to each personal data field.

   ```html
   <input name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email">
   <input name="name" autocomplete="name">
   ```

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.keyboard-navigation"></a>

### 3.11 Keyboard navigability

- Stable ID: `ia.keyboard-navigation`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Remove positive tabindex values and make custom controls focusable.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.keyboard-navigation)
- Evidence source: [MDN tabindex](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.keyboard-navigation`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.keyboard-navigation

Why: AI agents navigate pages using keyboard-style interactions via the accessibility tree. Positive tabindex values break natural focus order, and missing focusable elements on interactive widgets prevent AI agents from discovering and operating controls.

References:

- [MDN tabindex](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex) (guide)
- [W3C Focus Order](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order.html) (spec)

Steps:

1. Replace tabindex values above 0 with 0 or remove them.
2. Use native button and a elements, or add tabindex="0" and a role to custom controls.

   ```html
   <div role="button" tabindex="0">Open menu</div>
   ```

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.button-names"></a>

### 3.13 Button accessible names

- Stable ID: `ia.button-names`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Give each button a text or an aria-label.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.button-names)
- Evidence source: [WCAG Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.button-names`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.button-names

Why: AI agents invoke buttons by their accessible name in the accessibility tree. Without a discernible name, an AI agent cannot identify what a button does, making form submission and page interaction impossible.

References:

- [WCAG Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html) (spec)
- [MDN button element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/button) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add visible text to each button, or an aria-label for icon buttons.

   ```html
   <button type="button" aria-label="Close dialog"><svg aria-hidden="true">...</svg></button>
   ```

<a id="ia.aria-hidden"></a>

### 3.14 aria-hidden misuse

- Stable ID: `ia.aria-hidden`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Remove aria-hidden from the body and from focusable elements.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.aria-hidden)
- Evidence source: [MDN aria-hidden](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-hidden)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.aria-hidden`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.aria-hidden

Why: aria-hidden="true" removes elements from the accessibility tree. When applied to the <body> or to focusable elements, it corrupts the tree that AI agents navigate, causing them to miss content or encounter invisible controls.

References:

- [MDN aria-hidden](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-hidden) (guide)
- [WCAG Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html) (spec)

Steps:

1. Remove aria-hidden="true" from the body element.
2. Remove aria-hidden from links, buttons and inputs, or make them not focusable.

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.widget-state"></a>

### 3.15 Dynamic widget state

- Stable ID: `ia.widget-state`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Expose the state of interactive widgets with ARIA state attributes.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.widget-state)
- Evidence source: [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.widget-state`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.widget-state

Why: Agents operate interactive widgets through the accessibility tree. Expandable panels, tabs, menus, switches, dialogs, and async status areas need explicit state so agents can tell what is open, selected, checked, current, or updating.

References:

- [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/) (guide)
- [MDN ARIA states and properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes) (guide)
- [WCAG Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html) (spec)

Steps:

1. Add aria-expanded and aria-controls to disclosure buttons.

   ```html
   <button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="filters">Filters</button>
   <section id="filters" hidden>...</section>
   ```
2. Add aria-selected to tabs, aria-checked to switches and role="status" to async messages.

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.
